newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong shares set record, others in Asia gain.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong shares set record, others in Asia gain.

text.p: The Hang Seng Index set a record high on Friday after an overnight U.S. bond rally cheered Hong Kong investors, while buying by institutions helped end a two-day losing streak for Tokyo shares.
The Hang Seng index ended 51.71 points higher at a record close of 12,529.27. The previous record close was 12,510.05 reached on October 18.
"There is a very strong correlation between the Hang Seng index and the (long bond) yield," Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities, said.

The U.S. long bond surged on Thursday, pushing the yield down to 6.64 percent after the release of U.S. weekly jobless claims and Chicago purchasing managers data. The data suggested the inflation outlook remains tame.

"Overall we are still optimistic the market is poised to challenge the recent intra-day record high," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International. The intra-day record of 12,602.34 was set on October 16.
Tokyo stocks regained their footing with help from futures-linked trade in the afternoon, brokers said. The key Nikkei 225 ended 166.20 points, or 0.81 percent, higher at 20,633,06.
"Futures buying emerged late in the afternoon, stimulating cash stocks and bringing up the Nikkei average," a trader said
The benchmark was lifted in the morning by buying after it had posted hefty losses for two consecutive days.

"Investment trusts which were expected to buy on Thursday, but didn't, bought shares today, boosting the Nikkei average above the 20,500 level near the end of the session," said Akishige Ishikura, Dai-ichi Securities analyst.

Taiwan share prices finished higher on buying of blue-chip companies that reported sound profits in the first three quarters, brokers said. The weighted index ended up 29.02 points or 0.45 percent at 6,455.11.

Shares of some electronic companies led Friday's gain. "Today's buying in electronics is selective. It only concentrates on firms that showed sound profits," said Tank Hung, an analyst of Yuan Ta Securities.
In South Korea shares ended higher, led by active bargain hunting in small and medium-sized shares, brokers said.
"It's too early to say the market has turned around, it's more of a technical rebound from the eight-day fall we had," said Bae Kyoung-jin of Seoul Securities.
The market gained 10.28 points to provisionally end at 767.87.
Singapore shares closed lower on selling of large property companies. The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index ended 15.06 points lower at 2,068.17.
The dollar was trading at 113.71/3.76 yen and 1.5199/06 marks at 1115 GMT.
SIMEX Brent crude oil futures for December traded at $22.68 per barrel vs London's settlement of $22.69.
Gold bullion ended in Hong Kong at US$377.60/378.10 an ounce against New York's US$377.90/378.40.
